stage: Stage 2 - graph, first half: the input set and its staging
purpose: The per-project JAR inventory and the one-to-one staging manifest: together, the proof that every JAR the full-reactor build produced was actually supplied to the Joern bytecode frontend. Delivery of the input set is established HERE, by this manifest, and not by later searching the graph for a class per module - the graph is the thing being verified, so it cannot also be the verification (AAP 0.1.3). harness/cpg/spark.cpg names this file in its depends_on_files and is built over the single input path recorded here.
provenance: Written by clone 005 of the run, from the full-reactor build this clone performed. Every size and every sha256 in this file was computed from the bytes on disk by this clone, and no figure was carried over from the earlier build within the same run whose tree was deleted with the scratch directory of the clone that ran it.

clone.measurement_scratch_note: The build tree, the private Maven local repository and the measurement output live in this clone's private scratch directory, outside every repository checkout. The staging directory is inside the clone at harness/artifacts/cpg-input, which .gitignore:31 'artifacts/' keeps out of git's ordinary collection.
clone.artifact_tree_note: harness/artifacts/ is excluded from git's ordinary collection by .gitignore:31 'artifacts/'. This file is force-added, as the sibling evidence logs in the same directory are; the staged JARs under harness/artifacts/cpg-input/ are NOT committed - they are build output, and this manifest with its per-file byte size and sha256 is how that tree is published (AAP 0.1.1).

governing_rules.review_rules_result: review_rules with view_range [1,-1] returned exactly 'No user rules provided.' That is a complete read: no rules document exists for this project, which AAP 0.7 and 0.10.2 corroborate. The absence is stated rather than worked around, and it is not read as licence to lower the bar.
governing_rules.substitute_standard: Enterprise best practice held to the AAP's own four principles, restated here because they are what this file is judged against:

principles.name: Verification is independent of the thing verified
principles.applied_here: This file IS the independent verification of input delivery: the graph is not consulted to establish what was fed to the frontend. Inside the file the same principle recurses. The inventory is built from two independent directions - the Maven model's declarations and the filesystem - and reconciled. The manifest's own correctness is asserted as a one-to-one MAPPING, total and injective in both directions, never as a count plus a hash set: a set discards multiplicity, and this staged set actually contains 191 files over only 189 distinct digests, so a set-based check would balance even with one file staged twice and another omitted. Every staged file's digest was recomputed from the staged path, and staging is a copy rather than a hard link so that re-measurement reads independent bytes.

principles.name: Reject rather than infer
principles.applied_here: A file whose provenance could not be decided would be recorded as undecided with its evidence; 0 were. No winner map is emitted, because which input supplied the surviving definition of an overwritten class is not measurable from this frontend's output. Where a module has no class that is absent from every other module's artifacts, that is recorded as presence evidence and named as such, rather than presented as exclusivity.

principles.name: Halt-and-report over silent repair
principles.applied_here: A pre-existing staging directory is a halt, never cleared and never reused, because a stale JAR in it would silently enter the graph; the absence check and its transcript are recorded before creation. A staged-name collision, a digest mismatch between a source and its staged copy, and a mapping that is not total and injective in both directions each raise rather than being worked around. Nothing was trimmed from the input set to make a later count fit.

principles.name: Verbatim preservation
principles.applied_here: Filenames, paths and digests appear exactly as measured. Command transcripts carry their stdout, stderr and exit status unedited, including the failing ls whose failure is itself the measurement.

governing_rules.never_fabricate: No size and no digest in this file was written from any source other than reading the bytes. The spot-verifications in the checks below - including the fixed nine-file sample in check inventory.independent_spot_verification, which covers both non-root output cases and the root parent's attached artifact - were run with sha256sum and wc -c, which are not the code that built the inventory. The digests that build-reactor.log independently recorded for the same artifacts are a third measurement, and the cross-check compares them file by file.

verdict_vocabulary.note: The vocabulary the checks below draw on.
verdict_vocabulary.recorded_difference: observed differs from an expectation that is not an anchor, or from a prior provisioning's value. Both values are recorded with their provenance and the run continues (AAP 0.9.3).
verdict_vocabulary.halt: a condition AAP 0.9.2 stops the run on. None is present in this file; the halts list is empty.
verdict_vocabulary.inconclusive: the outcome could not be established; what was tried is recorded.

subject.version_at_that_commit: Spark 4.1.0-SNAPSHOT, Scala 2.13.17, Java 17, Maven 3.9.11 - read from the built tree's own pom at pom.xml:29, :178, :120, :123
subject.build_tree_note: A private clone of the pin, checked out by SHA, still at the pin and clean. It is the tree harness/artifacts/logs/build-reactor.log built and the only tree this inventory measures. It is NOT /opt/spark-src: that clone is host-global, shared with concurrent clones that read it while they scan, and carries a narrowed build with no artifact for tools, examples or any connector/kafka-0-10* module.

spark_src.role: the pinned clone every scanner targets. NOT the tree inventoried here and not written to by this file. The build present in it was narrowed with -pl to 33 projects and 32 JAR producers (harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 5), so it cannot answer a full-reactor question.

subject.build_verdict_cited: BUILD SUCCESS, Maven exit 0, 40 of 40 reactor projects SUCCESS, 0 FAILURE, 0 SKIPPED, 38 of 38 JAR-packaging projects confirmed on disk to have produced their own main artifact. Elapsed 2460 s, recorded as a fact rather than against a budget.

reactor_arithmetic.flag_note: Five flags, four added modules. -Pyarn (pom.xml:3384) adds resource-managers/yarn and common/network-yarn; -Pkubernetes (pom.xml:3392) adds resource-managers/kubernetes/core; -Phive-thriftserver (pom.xml:3407) adds sql/hive-thriftserver. -Phive resolves in sql/hive/pom.xml:209 and -Pvolcano in resource-managers/kubernetes/core/pom.xml:36; both are module-local, add no reactor entry, and change what gets compiled.

two_directions.direction_1_maven_model: Each project's own coordinates and packaging read from its pom - the first artifactId outside the <parent> block, so an inherited parent coordinate cannot be mistaken for the project's own - together with every output path a plugin declares explicitly, resolved through the properties that define it, each with its file:line locator.
two_directions.direction_2_filesystem: Every *.jar under that project's build directory, enumerated recursively, with its byte size and sha256 read from the file and its archive contents read from the archive.
two_directions.reconciliation: The two directions are reconciled per file: a filename coordinate or a declared output path decides provenance, and the archive's own META-INF/maven/**/pom.properties supplies the coordinate of anything excluded, where the archive states one.
two_directions.maven_not_invoked: No Maven goal was run to obtain the effective model. The local repository at /root/.m2/repository is shared read-only with concurrent clones and even an offline goal can write into it, so the model side was derived from the pom declarations plus the coordinates Maven itself wrote into each artifact's Maven descriptor. That is the effective model as the build recorded it, obtained without writing to a shared path.

why_location_is_not_provenance: examples/pom.xml:136 sends the project's MAIN artifact to ${jars.target.dir}, defined at pom.xml:265 as ${project.build.directory}/scala-${scala.binary.version}/jars, so its main artifact is not in its build directory's root.

common/network-yarn/pom.xml:37 defines ${shuffle.jar}, :96 sets <shadedArtifactAttached>false</shadedArtifactAttached> and :97 sets <outputFile>${shuffle.jar}</outputFile>, so its shaded shuffle JAR is neither in the build directory's root nor attached to the project, and its filename carries no artifactId at all.

pom.xml:3102 points the root pom's copy-module-dependencies execution (id at pom.xml:3095) at the very same ${jars.target.dir}, and core/pom.xml:529-552 and mllib/pom.xml:184-206 point their own copy-dependencies executions at ${project.build.directory} with useSubDirectoryPerType, which lands them in target/jars. So the same directories hold a project's own output and other projects' dependencies: provenance, not location, is what separates them.

classification_rule.own: the filename stem, after an optional 'original-' prefix is stripped, is exactly <artifactId>-<version> or begins with <artifactId>-<version>- (a classifier); OR the path is exactly an output path this project's own pom declares for its jar or shade plugin.
classification_rule.excluded: carries another coordinate and matches no output path this project declares. Sub-classified as copied_runtime_dependency when it sits under a directory this build declares as a dependency-copy target, or test_resource_fixture when it sits inside the module's compiled-output tree, i.e. a resource copied from src/ rather than an artifact the packaging phase produced.
classification_rule.undecided: neither could be established. Recorded with its evidence, never silently classified. 0 files fell here.
classification_rule.retained_without_exception: Nothing the project itself emitted is sampled or dropped: main artifacts, 'original-' pre-shade siblings, shaded siblings, classifier artifacts, -tests artifacts, -sources and -test-sources artifacts, and the unattached shaded shuffle JAR are all retained (AAP 0.5.1, 0.8.3). Whether an artifact carries bytecode is recorded per file as class_entry_count rather than used as a reason to drop it.
classification_rule.scope_of_the_walk: The enumeration is per-project and rooted at that project's build directory, so the JARs checked into the source tree under src/test/resources are outside it by construction - they are source files, not output the build produced.

not_done: It did not rebuild anything. A second build would be a second measurement of a fact build-reactor.log already established, which AAP 0.6.4 forbids, and its artifacts would carry different digests for no gain.
It did not write to /opt/spark-src, to the shared local repository, to the rulesets, to the feed caches, to the graph, or to the build tree it read. All are shared read-only with concurrent clones.

It did not trim the input set. No -tests artifact, no pre-shade sibling, no sources artifact and not the spark-connect-shims artifact was excluded, notwithstanding that the provisioning's own graph excluded some of them by runbook instruction; see recorded_differences.
It did not invoke the frontend, load the graph, or state any graph count. Those belong to cpg-frontend.log and cpg-verify.log.
It did not judge any finding, and no finding of any kind appears here.
It did not clear or reuse a staging directory, and it tore nothing down.

non_root_output_cases.note: The two artifacts a location-based rule loses. Both are asserted present at their resolved paths and both are in the staged input set.

exclusions.coordinate_source_method: For each excluded archive, whether it carries its own META-INF/maven/**/pom.properties descriptor (the coordinate is stated by the archive) or not (the coordinate is available from the filename alone). Measured by reading each archive's entry list.

staging.why_a_single_directory: The bundled jimple2cpg accepts ONE input path - a file or a directory, with --recurse to descend (AAP 0.2.2). 'Every JAR the build produced' and 'one input path' are reconciled by staging the inventory into a single directory and then proving the staged set IS the inventory.
absent_before_use_evidence: inventory.staging_absent_before_use in the checks array below
the staging script halts and exits non-zero if the directory exists, so a run that reached the copy step is a run that found it absent
staging.never_cleared_never_reused: A pre-existing staging tree is a halt (AAP 0.9.2): a stale JAR in it would silently enter the graph, and a graph's silence about a module is indistinguishable from a clean result.
staging.method: copy (shutil.copyfile), chosen over a hard link so the staged bytes are independent of the shared build tree and can be re-hashed as an independent measurement

root_project_slug.why: The reactor root project has no module path, so it cannot supply one. Its slug is the literal 'root'; no module slug equals it, which is asserted during staging rather than assumed, and a leading-dot alternative was rejected because a hidden file can be skipped by a recursive walk.

staging.ordering: The manifest is ordered by module path, then by the artifact's path relative to the build tree. The order is recorded so the input set is reproducible byte for byte (AAP 0.5.1).

staging.timestamp_source: The filesystem's own record of the staging pass, read with stat: the staging directory's birth time is when this run created it (having just found it absent), its mtime is when the last file was copied into it, and the measurement file's mtime below is when the bidirectional assertion was written. Recorded from stat rather than from a clock read while this document was generated, so the times are the staging pass's own.

assertion.statement: Every inventory entry maps to exactly one staged name and one sha256, and every file found in the staging directory maps back to exactly one inventory entry. The mapping is required TOTAL and INJECTIVE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.
assertion.why_not_a_count_and_a_hash_set: A set discards multiplicity, so two different multisets can share both a count and a hash set (AAP 0.5.1). This staged set is a live example: 191 files over 189 distinct digests, with 2 collision group(s). A set-based check would compare 191 to 191 and 189 to 189 and pass even if one file had been staged twice and another omitted.

staged_digest_reverification.method: every staged file re-hashed by reading the staged path, from the directory listing rather than from the manifest, so a file the manifest does not name would surface

assertion.halt_rule: AAP 0.9.2: a staging manifest that is not total and injective in both directions against the inventory halts the run. It is not repaired by adding or removing a file.
assertion.computed_at_source: the mtime of the measurement file the assertion was written to, read with stat

determinism.duplicate_class_names_are_deliberate: This input set contains duplicate class names by design. Shaded JARs vendor the same third-party classes, each module contributes both its shaded artifact and its 'original-' pre-shade sibling which duplicate every class between them, and the spark-connect-shims artifact ships stub SparkConf, SparkContext and RDD classes that core and the SQL modules also ship.
determinism.frontend_behaviour: The frontend extracts the inputs into one layout WITH REPLACEMENT, so some definitions win and others are discarded.
determinism.what_is_reproducible: The ordered staging manifest is persisted in this file, so the input set is reproducible byte for byte: the same 191 files, the same staged names, the same digests, in the same order.
determinism.what_is_not_measurable: WHICH input won a given collision is NOT measurable from this frontend's output. The frontend's directory walk is not ordered by this run, and its overwrite report names the destination class rather than the JAR that supplied the surviving definition. This document therefore does not promise a winner map.
determinism.winner_map: NOT EMITTED. A populated winner map would be an inference presented as a measurement, which is exactly the 'reject rather than infer' violation. What is recorded instead, by cpg-frontend.log, is the observed overwrite count and the affected classes; where a specific collision matters to a conclusion it is resolved by querying the graph for that class and reporting what is there.
determinism.consequence: Because delivery is proved by the one-to-one manifest above, duplicate class names are a DETERMINISM question rather than a COVERAGE question. That is the only reason the limitation stated here is acceptable.

class_entry_observations.duplication_note: The input set holds far more class ENTRIES than distinct class NAMES; the difference is the duplication described above, and it is what the frontend resolves by replacement.
class_entry_observations.note: Per-artifact class-entry counts are recorded on each inventory entry. The graph-side overwrite and AST-failure counts are cpg-frontend.log's to measure, not this file's, and none is predicted here.

coverage_witness_inputs.ownership: oss-scan-results/build-record.md owns the per-module coverage VERDICT. This section records the inputs that verdict is derived from, measured over the artifacts inventoried here.
coverage_witness_inputs.test: A class present in that module's PRIMARY artifact - its main unclassified, non-'original-', non-'-tests' JAR - and absent from every other module's artifacts. A class shared with a same-module sibling still qualifies, which is what makes the test satisfiable for a shaded/pre-shade pair; a class shared with another module does not.
coverage_witness_inputs.weaker_witness: Where no such class exists, the module-exclusive META-INF/maven/**/pom.properties file node is accepted and named as the weaker witness.
coverage_witness_inputs.prohibited_substitute: A shared package prefix is never evidence. Every Spark module shares org.apache.spark, so a prefix test lets one module vouch for a dozen absent ones (AAP 0.1.1). No prefix test is used anywhere in this file.
coverage_witness_inputs.measurement_basis: Class sets read from the archives themselves: 67135 distinct class names across the 191 own artifacts, 45501 across the primary artifacts alone, from 99723 class entries in total.

selection_rules.injective_witness: where classes unique to the module exist, the witness reported is the lexicographically first of them
selection_rules.presence_evidence: where none exists, the class reported is the least-shared class of the primary artifact; among equally-shared classes one in org/apache/spark/ is preferred, then lexicographic order. The rule is total, so the choice is reproducible rather than incidental to dict ordering, and the count of modules it is shared with is recorded beside it

coverage_witness_inputs.ubiquitous_class_note: Exactly 1 class name is shipped by 20 or more modules: org/apache/spark/unused/UnusedStubClass, in 35 of them. It comes from Spark's org.spark-project.spark:unused stub dependency and is named here so its ubiquity is not mistaken for a measurement error - it is also why several modules' shared-class counts read as 1 against nearly every other module.
